precepts.text: Remember Lot's wife: you are in this truth now, stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to please everybody and dropping by on birthdays, stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed as she was.
precepts.point: He overthrew the cities and all the plain, and Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt; why look back at a city like that unless you were not vexed with it and missed something in it?
precepts.why:
The angels pulled Lot into the house and smote the men at the door with blindness, and even blinded they wearied themselves trying to find the door. Then the angels took Lot out and gave them one order as the cities burned: don't look back. “And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.” “But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.”

Why would she look back? The city was being destroyed; she had just seen what happened in front of her house. She should have been glad to escape. Somebody was not vexed with the filthy conversation of that city; there was something in it she missed. That is why Luke also says, if you put your hand on the plow and look back, you are not worthy.

Christ said it in three words: “Remember Lot’s wife.” That is a warning for all of us: don't look back. You are in this truth now. Stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to be friends with everybody and please people, stop dropping by the house on their birthday. Focus on this truth and stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed just as Lot's wife was destroyed.

Judgment is coming to Esau, as Sodom's came. “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” We have to come out of her mentally, come back to the law, statutes and commandments, stop playing around in the truth, and keep the faith of Christ, without looking back.

precepts.text: Brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven: that is how Sodom and Gomorrah went, and that is how this Babylon goes.
precepts.point: It is destined to be burned with fire, which is the weapons Christ is coming with, and Revelation says she shall be utterly burned with fire.

precepts.text: Neither had any man known her proves that to know means intercourse.
precepts.point: The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness.
precepts.why:
The men of Sodom called for the men who came in to Lot, “that we may know them.” To know in scripture is to lie with. Rebekah “was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her.” A virgin is one no man has known, so to know means intercourse.

That is what the men of Sodom wanted with the men in Lot’s house, and it was not a few of them. “Both old and young, all the people from every quarter” compassed the house. The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness.

precepts.text: Sodom and Gomorrah, giving themselves to fornication and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.
precepts.point: Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.
precepts.why:
When Lot entered Zoar, “the Lord rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven.” Jude says why that overthrow is written: “Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.”

They gave themselves over to fornication and went after strange flesh, and they are set forth for an example. What was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands.

Notice too that the angel could not act until Lot was out: “Haste thee, escape thither; for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither.” The destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, the same way the angels in Revelation 7 hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed.

precepts.text: The cities were made an example unto those that after should live ungodly, and just Lot was delivered.
precepts.point: Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.
precepts.why:
The Lord, “turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly.” The brimstone and fire that overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants and that which grew upon the ground, is an ensample for the ungodly who come after.

“And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)” Lot had found grace in His sight, and the Lord would not do any thing till he was come to Zoar.

A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct. Lot lived among them and it vexed his righteous soul from day to day, and just Lot was delivered.

precepts.text: The standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul; the wasteland that smoketh is a testimony to this day.
precepts.point: Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.
precepts.why:
Wisdom “delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.” And the marks of that wickedness remain: “even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.”

Lot’s wife looked back, against the instruction, and “she became a pillar of salt.” That pillar is a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. She was brought out with the righteous, and her look back showed where her heart still was.

precepts.text: As it was in the days of Lot, so shall it be in the day the Son of man is revealed; remember Lot's wife.
precepts.point: Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.
precepts.why:
“Remember Lot’s wife.” Three words, among the weightiest in the scriptures. Christ sets the days of Lot as the pattern for the day He is revealed: “they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded; But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all. Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.”

In that day, he on the housetop with his stuff in the house is not to come down to take it, and he in the field is not to return back. Then: “Remember Lot’s wife.” She looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt.

If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot’s wife.

precepts.text: The nakedness of thy father and mother thou shalt not uncover; incest is against the law of the Most High.
precepts.point: The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.
precepts.why:
Lot’s daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and “there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us”, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him, and “he perceived not when she lay down, nor when she arose.” Do not take any wayward idea from this. “The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover.” Uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now.

Out of it came two nations: the firstborn bare Moab, “the father of the Moabites unto this day”, and the younger bare Benammi, “the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.” Those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.
